tasks.title: Monitoring and three nines
tasks.statement: The service runs without monitoring, and users report outages before you notice them. Add monitoring (metrics, logs, alerts) and bring the design up to an availability target of 99.9% with p99 of at most 120 ms. Right now there is a single database, and it drags availability down.
tasks.hint: Put the “Monitoring” component on the diagram (no links needed). For 99.9% the database must have a replica and automatic failover.

tasks.title: SLO 99.95%: cheaply
tasks.statement: The availability target is 99.95%. Build the cheapest design that meets it: monitoring is required, the design survives failure of the database and of an app server, and the budget is $700 per month.
tasks.hint: A single load balancer caps availability at 99.95%, so you need two. An S database with a replica and automatic failover, two or three M servers.

tasks.title: Five nines
tasks.statement: For a payment gateway the target is availability of at least 99.999%. Every component must be redundant: load balancers, app servers and the database. Build a design with monitoring and a budget of $1500 per month that reaches the target and survives the failure of any component.
tasks.hint: Two load balancers, three servers, and a database with two replicas and automatic failover give about 99.9999%.

tasks.title: Capacity headroom
tasks.statement: The monitoring team set an alert at 60% load: anything higher is a reason to worry. The load is 1500 reads and 200 writes per second. Bring the design to a state where no component is loaded above 60%, with monitoring and a budget of $1300 per month.
tasks.hint: Servers: 1700 requests — two L (3000, 57%). An M database at 1500 reads is at 83%: you need a replica or size L.

tasks.title: The latency budget
tasks.statement: Latency SLO: p50 of at most 40 ms and p99 of at most 80 ms. There are 2700 reads per second, the M database is almost at its limit, and the app servers build up a queue under high load. Add a cache (≥80%) and reduce server load to meet the targets.
tasks.hint: Latency grows as 1/(1 − load): keep the servers at about 50%. A 5 GB cache with TTL 3600 takes the reads off the database.

tasks.title: A design with reliability targets
tasks.statement: The chapter's final exercise. A service with SLOs: availability ≥ 99.995%, p99 ≤ 100 ms, load at most 60%. It gets 3000 reads and 150 writes per second. Build a design with monitoring: two load balancers, a cache with a replica, a database with a replica and automatic failover, survival of failure of the database, the cache and an app server, and a budget of $2200 per month.
tasks.hint: About nine M servers (load ~50%), a 6 GB cache with a replica and TTL 3600, an M database with a replica and automatic failover, and monitoring.
